messages.subject: Sorry!
parts:
Hi again,

 

Sorry, I looked at a damaged weather.csv in Excel. The “RainToday” and the “RainTomorrow” columns are adjusted one step in the original one.

 

How to make a prediction for 2 days in advance? Is it done by adjusting the target column 2 steps?

 

What is the difference between classification and regression? I don’t see where to choose between them in Rattle. Is the choice made automatic?

 

Kind regards

Rolf

Sorry, I looked at a damaged weather.csv in Excel. The “RainToday” and the “RainTomorrow” columns are adjusted one step in the original one.

I simply process the data to add RainTomorrow from tomorrow's information! You could easily change that to add RainTomorrow2 for 2 days ahead, etc.

In building the model it only looks at today's conditions to predict rain tomorrow. No "time series" in the simple model.

Decided on the Data tab depending on Target variable see Target Data Type.
 

Kind regards

Rolf

Thanks for the suggestion Ajay. Rattle does not (yet?) have a plugin framework. However, from a programming point of view it is quite straightforward to add such new functionality. 

The key is to work out the "use case" or scenario, end to end. I.e., Where do the time series options best sit within the GUI, how do we identify the variable roles in the Data tab, what Evaluate tab changes are needed, etc. Given such a scenario, and the example R code I can look to add support for time series (a bit like the survival analysis options).

Regards,
Graham

Hi Dr Graham,

 I was looking into Rwidgets/ playwith etc but felt that Time Series Models are best suited in Rattle (also surprisingly during my extensive research on R GUIs only RKWard has a Time Series Component- but no stable Windows release)

Basically only three parameters p,d,q need to be changed in the Arima model with seasonality as well as fourth parameter.

The code needs to use (for starters)-

ibrary(tseries)

air <- AirPassengers #Datasetname

ts.plot(air)

acf(air)

pacf(air)

plot(decompose(air))

air.fit <- arima(air,order=c(0,1,1), seasonal=list(order=c(0,1,1), period=12)) #The ARIMA Model 

tsdiag(air.fit)

library(forecast)

air.forecast <- forecast(air.fit)

plot.forecast(air.forecast)

THE ONLY PARAMETERS are Arima (P,D,Q) and Period =Pwhich are given in code in #The ARIMA MODEL as (0,0,1) and period=12

http://decisionstats.com
http://dudeofdata.com

On Thu, Oct 21, 2010 at 3:47 AM, Bob Muenchen <muench...@gmail.com> wrote:
On 10/20/2010 6:22 AM, Ajay Ohri wrote:
Hi Dr Graham,

I was looking into Rwidgets/ playwith etc but felt that Time Series Models are best suited in Rattle (also surprisingly during my extensive research on R GUIs only RKWard has a Time Series Component- but no stable Windows release)

Hi Ajay,

I hope I'm not abusing the rattle-users group by telling  you that R Commander does indeed offer a time series plug-in:
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RcmdrPlugin.epack/index.html

Cheers,
Bob

Basically only three parameters p,d,q need to be changed in the Arima model with seasonality as well as fourth parameter.

The code needs to use (for starters)-

ibrary(tseries)

air <- AirPassengers #Datasetname

ts.plot(air)

acf(air)

pacf(air)

plot(decompose(air))

air.fit <- arima(air,order=c(0,1,1), seasonal=list(order=c(0,1,1), period=12)) #The ARIMA Model 

tsdiag(air.fit)

library(forecast)

air.forecast <- forecast(air.fit)

plot.forecast(air.forecast)

          
THE ONLY PARAMETERS are Arima (P,D,Q) and Period =Pwhich are given in code in #The ARIMA MODEL as (0,0,1) and period=12

On Wed, Oct 20, 2010 at 9:08 AM, Graham Williams <Graham....@togaware.com> wrote:
Thanks for the suggestion Ajay. Rattle does not (yet?) have a plugin framework. However, from a programming point of view it is quite straightforward to add such new functionality.

The key is to work out the "use case" or scenario, end to end. I.e., Where do the time series options best sit within the GUI, how do we identify the variable roles in the Data tab, what Evaluate tab changes are needed, etc. Given such a scenario, and the example R code I can look to add support for time series (a bit like the survival analysis options).

Regards,
Graham
